question: TypeSafe (Jev) neden tezgah'ta hiç kullanılmıyor, hangi yüzeylerde kullanılabilir, ve token/maliyet/hız açısından ne kazandırır?

evaluation.metric: measured token cost of one app-analysis screen read through the wired Playwright MCP, the always-on text tezgah injects per session (the installer's own context budget), and - added 2026-09-22 - the recall of the load-bearing control lines a judgement keeps at a given read share, plus the wrong-load count of the roster-compaction arms
evaluation.baseline: one 40-row admin screen read = 14,805 chars (~3,701 tokens); a two-screen flow = 15,943 chars (~3,985 tokens); a real docs page = 22,193 chars (~5,548 tokens); tezgah always-on = 7,545 chars core + 8,019 chars skill roster per session (2026-09-20; 8,380 + 9,168 over 14 skills on 2026-09-22); the per-line triage shape = 69.9% of 83 control lines at a 26.4% read, the shipped unit shape = 100% at a 94% read; the compact roster = 1/20 and 2/20 wrong loads against 0/20 for the full roster
evaluation.note: measured after the questions were fixed in findings.md. The note originally said the predictions were still untested; two of them were run afterwards - P1 is refuted by the per-line triage (69.9% recall) and P2's saving is measured and refused by the compaction arms - while P3 and P4 stay unrun. The recall and compaction metrics were added to this evaluation on 2026-09-22, when the line was closed against a tree that has since built five of the six surfaces.

hypotheses: H1: TypeSafe is absent because tezgah has no model-calling layer, not because the capability was judged useless. Confirmed: hooks/ contains no HTTP client, and the only TypeSafe code is a health row that checks omp's key.

H2: the credential is unreachable from tezgah's own code. Confirmed: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not exported in this environment; the key lives in omp's private store (~/.omp/agent/agent.db, auth_credentials.data), and tezgah's documented ~/.config/typesafe/key is explicitly not what omp opens.

H3: the cost lever is not tezgah's own rules (regex, free) but what the agent reads into its context, where one screen read is 3.7k tokens at the expensive model's price. Partly confirmed by measurement; the saving a TypeSafe triage would produce is untested (see protocol.md).

H4: TypeSafe must stay out of the gate/integrity/consent path, where refusal reproducibility is an invariant the tests pin. Confirmed by reading tezgah_gate/tezgah_integrity and the test suite's hermetic style.

events.what: the user observes TypeSafe is still unused in tezgah and asks for a comprehensive analysis of the skills, the app-analysis surface and anywhere else it applies, with the goal of cutting cost and tokens and gaining speed.
inventoried every TypeSafe reference in the repo: one health row (hooks/tezgah_paths.py:213, surfaced by bin/tezgah-setup:2074) plus its tests; no call path anywhere.
measured the read cost of an app analysis with the pinned Playwright MCP: 14,805 chars for one 40-row admin screen, 15,943 chars for a two-screen flow, 22,193 chars for a real page.

measured tezgah's own always-on text from the installer's budget report: 7,545 chars core, 8,019 chars skill roster, 891 chars subagent briefs, 961 chars per-turn reminder, 5,053 chars conditional rules.

read TypeSafe's live docs: economics ($0.042/1M input, $0 output), the batching result (12.2x cheaper, 10.0x faster), re-ranking, line-by-line search, and the skill-suggestion cookbook with its 488-request measurement.
six surfaces where a judgment would pay, and four places it must not go; the credential path and the offline invariant are left as decisions for the user.

measured the per-line triage shape live (tezgah-triage --select on a 356-line / 13,045-char admin screen): 94 lines selected (26.4%), 13,559 input tokens, $0.000569, recall 58 of 83 load-bearing controls = 69.9% - prediction P1's 95% floor refuted, which is C6-R.

ran the four-arm roster-compaction experiment over 28 labelled prompts on an independent chooser with TypeSafe as a biased secondary: wrong loads 0/20 (full), 0/20 (full+line), 1/20 (compact), 2/20 (compact+line), no discordant pair favouring compaction - so the ~1,516 tokens are refused, which is C7. Cost $0.0504.

closed the line on 2026-09-22 against the tree at HEAD ddf72b4: hooks/tezgah_judge.py is the seam and five of the six ranked surfaces are built as its callers (bin/tezgah-triage, tezgah-triage --states, bin/tezgah-docs, hooks/tezgah_skill_pick.py), the always-on roster measures 8,380 chars core plus 9,168 chars over 14 skills, and the claims the movement invalidates are superseded (C1-seam-exists, C4-secondary-economics, C5-picker-built, C6-unit-shape).
